finding: A user who holds workflows::manage/install but NOT mcp_servers::read is left with a PERMANENTLY disabled Tool field carrying a false 'Looking up this server…' placeholder and no stated reason. Chain: mcpServer/actions/loadMcpServers.ts:17 returns early without setting isInitialized OR error when hasPermissionNow(McpServersRead) is false, so serversInitialized=false and serversError=null forever; ToolStepForm.tsx:134 `serversSettled` is therefore false forever; entryForServerName (ToolCatalog.store.ts:428) returns {kind:'resolving-server', needsLookup:false} because listReady is false, so resolveServer is never called; ToolStepForm.tsx:191 `busy` stays true, :188-189 classifies resolving-server as transient so NO Alert renders, and :407 `disabled={busy}` disables the free-text escape hatch. Given a saved tool step and that permission set, the author can neither pick nor type a tool name, forever, with no explanation — the documented no-permission failure (ToolCatalog.store.ts:235-246 / :302-309) is unreachable because it needs a serverId the list can never supply. INV-6 violated (silent, non-degrading).

The drift guard can still pass VACUOUSLY. The lexer keys on the literal identifier `ValidationError` (validate.rs:2236) and reports the two ways to rename the type (`use … as VE`, `type VE = …`), but not the idiomatic third: `Self`. `impl ValidationError` exists at validate.rs:450, so a future convenience constructor written inside it — e.g. `pub(crate) fn dead_tools(loc:&str)->Self{ Self::at("semantic","WORKFLOW_NEW_CODE","…",loc) }` or a bare `Self { layer:…, code:"WORKFLOW_NEW_CODE", … }` — emits a real code that the scanner never sees. Because the code is also absent from VALIDATION_CODES and from HUMAN_COPY, all three assertions in validation_codes_are_registered_and_humanised agree: `unregistered` is empty (it was never scanned), `stale` is empty (it was never registered), `unhumanised` is empty (it was never registered). Guard green, raw wire message ships to the author. Same class as the alias hole round 2 closed; `<ValidationError>::err(…)` is a second (contrived) instance — the ident is followed by `>` not `::`, so scan_validation_error_use returns at :2385 treating it as a type mention.

Author-facing copy is humanised TWICE and the second pass truncates it. WorkflowBuilder.store.ts:410 already stores the humanised sentence (humaniseRequestError → humaniseValidatorFinding returns the full `Step N · label: <copy>` string, untidied). BuilderValidationPanel.tsx:98 then calls humaniseInstallError(store.error, steps) on that already-humanised string, and WorkflowBuilderPage.tsx:93 does the same on the re-thrown e.message for the toast. Second pass: no `[layer/CODE]` head → no status → falls to tidyMachineText (validationCopy.ts:447) which clips at MAX_ERROR_CHARS=160. Measured: WORKFLOW_BAD_STEP_ID copy is 190 chars, WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE 165, WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE 148 (+~26 for the 'Step N · label: ' prefix = 174). So a save that fails on any of these renders, in BOTH the Alert title and the toast, e.g. 'Step 2 · Fetch notes: The file this step reads its wording from ends up outside the workflow once the location is followed — point it at a file that is really …' — the actionable half is cut off. The docstring at :505 ('Idempotent: an already-humanised sentence passes through unchanged') is false for any copy over 160 chars.

fieldForValue still ERASES a stored `null` element of a multiselect argument — the exact data-loss class it was added to close. staleOption returns early for `value === null` (toolSchemaForm.ts:462); that guard is correct for the single-select case ('no value ⇒ no synthetic') but wrong for the per-ELEMENT call at :505, where null is a real array member. Given `arguments: {tags: ["a", null]}` against a schema declaring `items.enum: ["a","b"]` (hand-authored YAML, or an upstream schema that dropped null from the enum): no synthetic option is built for null, optionKeysForValues (:440-446) drops it via the `.filter(v => v !== undefined)`, the MultiSelect's value list becomes ["a"], and the next toggle rebuilds `arguments` from that list (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:299) — null is gone from the saved workflow. Contradicts DEC-6's rule that a value the current schema does not declare must survive editing. (A DECLARED null enum member is fine: enumOptions gives it raw null and matchOption finds it.)

The SERVER picker silently drops a configured value it cannot offer — the defect this branch fixed for the Tool picker (storedToolMissing synthetic option, ToolStepForm.tsx:201-217) and left standing one field above. CapabilitySelect (capabilities.tsx:14-21) builds its options from McpServer.servers — a PAGE of 10 (mcpServer/state.ts:11 pageSize:10, shared server-side search/status filters with /settings/mcp-servers) — and additionally `.filter(s => s.enabled)`. The kit Select renders the placeholder when `value` is not in `options` (select.tsx:148-176: customDisplay = selectedOpt?.label → undefined → SelectValue falls back to the placeholder). So for a saved step whose server is DISABLED, or is on page 2+, or is filtered out by a search term the user left on the MCP settings page, the required Server field reads 'Select a server' with no error (configErrors passes: step.server is non-empty) — while the new catalog Alert immediately below names that very server ('"X" is one of your servers but it is currently disabled'). Self-contradicting surface, and with >10 accessible servers the author cannot select the ones past page 1 at all (INV-3's job-to-be-done step 1). capabilities.tsx is untouched by this diff, but the disabled-server state that makes the contradiction visible is new here.

A stale SAVE error is never retired, so a provably-false finding sentence sits above a green 'No blocking errors.' createValidateRunner's success branch clears `error` only when `d.errorSource === 'validate'` (WorkflowBuilder.store.ts:122-126), and save() only clears it when the author retries the save (:370-374). Sequence: Save fails with `[semantic/WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING] agent_1: …` → store.error = 'Step 1 · Research the topic: This step needs a task description…', errorSource='save'. The author then fills the task in → updateStep → scheduleValidate → the check succeeds with zero errors. BuilderValidationPanel now renders the red Alert with that (now untrue) sentence at :141-152 AND the green 'No blocking errors.' at :164-169, because checkFailed is false. The panel added a staleness qualifier for the failed-CHECK case but there is none for a superseded save failure, and Save is enabled — so the only actionable text on screen is wrong.

A one-frame ENABLED free-text fallback flashes on the server-resolution boundary. On the frame where serverId first resolves, `entry` is still `EMPTY` (ToolCatalog.store.ts:418 `byServerId[match.id] ?? EMPTY`) — no failure, loading:false — so ToolStepForm.tsx:192 computes usePicker=false and :191 busy=false, rendering the hand-entry Input enabled with the generic 'The exact name of the tool to call on that server.' description and 'e.g. search' placeholder. The `load` effect (:161-166) is a useEffect, so it runs after paint; only then does loading:true flip the field to disabled and finally to the picker. The author briefly sees the INV-6 escape hatch presented as the normal state, with no reason given, for a state that is not a failure at all. Same one-frame path on every remount of an already-cached step form (StepConfigPanel keys the form by step id, so each step switch remounts with an empty local byServerId).

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT: the stored in-flight promise cannot produce an unhandled rejection or a permanently-pending entry. fetchTools (:198-213) and lookupServer (:274-282) each wrap the whole body in try/catch and RESOLVE with an entry/verdict, so `toolsPending`/`serversPending` never hold a rejected promise, however many late joiners await them. The generation guard (:260, :321) discards a superseded response, and `invalidate`/`invalidateServer` (:335-361) delete the pending entry and the local state together, so the invalidating instance cannot be left stuck on loading:true. The only way to strand a store instance at loading:true is a SECOND live ToolStepForm mount invalidating while the first awaits — unreachable, since StepConfigPanel.tsx:88 mounts exactly one step form (`key={step.id}`).

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT: the WeakMap scope key is stable. defineLocalStore.use memoises {api, proxy} in a useRef (store-kit.ts:630-645) and returns the SAME proxy object for every render of a mount, so `sessions` (ToolCatalog.store.ts:98) is keyed once per builder editing session rather than churning per render; sessionState never reads a prop off the proxy, so no hook is invoked by using it as a key; and the entry is collectable when the page unmounts. One fetch per server per session, as documented.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT: the number commit-on-blur is correct, and no pending edit is lost on unmount. Verified against the kit: InputNumber forwards its ref through Input (input.tsx:23,47) to the DOM input, and handleBlur (input-number.tsx:54-67) restores the previous text via setBuf BEFORE calling onBlur — React has not flushed it, so numberInput.current.value still holds what the author typed. Abandoned partial buffer ('-', '1e') → the raw read is non-empty → the argument is left alone; genuinely emptied box → buf==='' takes neither kit branch, the raw read is '' → commit(undefined) deletes the key. Unmount-before-blur is not reachable through the builder's own affordances: the step rows, Save, the tool Combobox and the ref menu all move focus (or focus body), which fires blur — and its commit lands on the store by step id before the click handler re-keys the panel.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT: the JSON/textarea commit-on-blur cannot lose data. onChange already commits the author's exact text on every keystroke (:317), so an unmount before blur leaves the text intact in `arguments`; only the JSON.parse coercion is deferred, and coerceToDeclared keeps an unparseable buffer as the raw string rather than nulling it (toolSchemaForm.ts:591-601). sameValue (:69-72) keeps a bare blur from marking the workflow dirty.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT: template mode does not desync. The latch is seeded from the value on mount (:108-110), re-latched whenever the value becomes a reference, and cleared only on a BLANK value (:127) so a half-typed '{{ inputs.limit' still holds the mode. It cannot outlive a step switch or a tool switch: StepConfigPanel.tsx:88 remounts the form per step, and the field key is `${toolKey}::${field.name}` (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:391) so a same-named property on a different tool gets a fresh instance. An external `arguments` replacement mid-edit cannot happen while the author has edits (WorkflowBuilder.store.ts:196 refuses to overwrite a dirty def); when it does happen the value change reaches the effect and clears/relatches correctly. Text/textarea/json never switch modes (canHoldTemplate, :97-98), which is the round-1 collapse fixed.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT (except the null case logged separately): a synthetic option cannot shadow a declared one nor be committed as declared. staleOption disambiguates its key against the list it will JOIN (`seen`, including earlier synthetics) with a suffix loop (:466-470), fieldForValue puts extras FIRST (:509) and matchOption's identity pass (`o.raw === value`, :408) resolves the stored value to the synthetic before any lenient key match, and optionValueForKey returns the option's `raw` (:434-437) so what is committed is the original stored value, unchanged. assignKeys (:257-270) keeps `enum:[1,"1"]` injective. Round-trips through save/reload because the value is never rewritten.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT: createValidateRunner's sequence guard has no ordering hole. `seq !== issued` is re-checked on BOTH the success and the failure path (:119, :129) so a superseded run can neither write a stale `validation` nor a stale error, and `validating` cannot stick — only the newest run clears it, and it is set true before every issue. errorSource routing is right in both directions: a successful check clears only a 'validate' error (:122-126) and a failed check refuses to overwrite a 'save' error (:135). The Save gate reads `validation` which can be up to one debounce window stale, but the backend re-validates on install and the failure is humanised, so no invalid workflow can be installed through the gap.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT (except the truncation logged separately): humaniseRequestError cannot blank a message, cannot leak an `HTTP error!` blob and does not mangle a validator finding. Every path ends in a non-empty string (`tidyMachineText(raw) || fallback`, :496); an HTTP-error string whose status maps to nothing returns the fallback rather than the response body (:495); parseInstallError's location regex (:364) requires an unspaced token followed by ': ', so a location-less message such as 'step has neither prompt: nor prompt_file:' cannot be mis-split (the anchored \S+ cannot reach the colon past the first space) and degrades to workflow-level, which is what it already is; and a code with no HUMAN_COPY entry returns null so the raw text is never re-attributed to a step it does not belong to.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT: no Rules-of-Hooks violation in the changed surfaces. StepList hoists attributeFindings/indexFindingsByStep above the `.map()` (:39-42) and reads no store field inside it; BuilderValidationPanel reads store.validation/validating/def/error/errorSource unconditionally at the top (:88-104) and attributes once before both lists; ToolStepForm reads McpServer.servers/isInitialized/error as three separate unconditional statements (:130-134) precisely so the hook count cannot vary with isInitialized; GeneratedField's hooks (useState/useEffect/useRef) are all unconditional and `control()` contains none; WorkflowBuilderPage destructures the store proxy at :49-59, before the `!canAccess` early return at :101.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT: the by-name lookup's wire contract holds. ListAccessibleServersQuery (server/src/modules/mcp/handlers/user.rs:44-53) takes page/per_page/search/status with no upper clamp or rejection on per_page, so SERVER_LOOKUP_PAGE_SIZE=100 is accepted and repository::list_accessible applies it directly; `search` is a server-side ILIKE over name/display_name/description, and lookupServer still requires exact `s.name === serverName` (:275) so a substring hit cannot be mistaken for the server. listTools' `res.tools ?? []` matches the optional wire field, and ValidationError.severity's optionality is handled defensively in severityOf (validationCopy.ts:258).

CHECKED, NOT LOGGED AS DEAD CODE: the `no-permission` branches in load (:235-246) and resolveServer (:302-309) are effectively unreachable — both require a resolved serverId / a listReady=true gate that only a user who already holds mcp_servers::read can produce, so they only fire on a mid-session permission revocation. They are legitimate defensive code, not dead weight; their unreachability is a symptom of the HIGH finding above (the permission-denied user never gets far enough to be told why), not a separate defect. Everything else new is wired: HUMANISED_CODES is consumed by humaniseValidatorFinding and by the gallery boot gate, WORKFLOW_LEVEL by indexFindingsByStep, ValidationSlice/ValidateRunnerDeps by the extracted runner, and all four new gallery surfaces are registered with the listTools cassette key.

CHECKED, GENUINELY WIRED: the tool-step surfaces run the production path, not a stub. toolStepSchemaSurface renders the real StepConfigPanel → ToolStepForm → ToolArgumentsForm against a resolvable server name, and the cassette adds the real `McpServerRuntime.listTools` key so ToolCatalogStoreDef.load actually fetches; the fallback surface points at a name the accessible list does not contain so entryForServerName reaches the stated-reason alert; and the fixture-code gate (throwing when a fixture code is absent from HUMANISED_CODES) makes the invented-code regression that hid the original defect impossible to reintroduce. The broken-def fixture's findings are consistent with the def they describe.

CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT: the Combobox re-select guard (`if (v === (step.tool ?? '')) return`, :387-390) does prevent Base UI's re-press of the highlighted row from wiping every filled-in argument, and the deliberate wipes (server change :336-341, genuine tool change) are correct — keeping server A's arguments on server B's tool would be worse. The free-row/generated-field merge order is also sound: commitField deletes the colliding row key before patching (:320) so the typed control wins while the row is still being edited, and absorbDeclaredRow drops the row on blur (:303-308) so the two editors never both own a key.

CONSIDERED AND DISMISSED as not worth logging: two theoretical option-mapping edges. (a) A schema declaring the empty string as an enum member cannot be committed — the kit Select treats '' as no-selection (select.tsx:92) and commitField deletes on '' — but an empty-string enum member is not a shape real MCP servers emit. (b) A stored multiselect array holding both 1 and "1" against `enum:[1,2]` maps both to the same control key, so the MultiSelect momentarily shows a duplicate chip until the next toggle normalises it to the declared type; that is the documented lenient re-selection working as intended, and requires an already-malformed stored value. Neither is a reachable user-facing failure.
